testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Do not base your gear shift decision on:

options.text: What the vehicle next to you is doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: What the vehicle next to you is doing.
questions.explanation: Shift gears based on your engine's rpm range and your speed. Learn when to shift up by checking your engine rpm or speedometer. Do not shift based on other vehicles around you.

questions.question: When traction is poor, accelerate slowly to:

options.text: Stay in control of your vehicle.
Stay behind the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in control of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Accelerate slowly on slippery roads. Too much speed or power can cause you to lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: What is Gross Combination Weight?

options.text: The total weight of the truck, trailer, and cargo.
The weight of a vehicle with no load.
The maximum weight the manufacturer allows.

questions.correctAnswerText: The total weight of the truck, trailer, and cargo.
questions.explanation: Gross Combination Weight is the total weight of the powered truck, trailer, and all cargo being carried.

questions.question: How do you test hydraulic brakes?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal three times. Then press firmly for five seconds. The pedal should not move.
Pump the brake pedal three times. Then press firmly for five seconds. The pedal should move slowly down.
Pump the brake pedal three times. Then press firmly for five seconds. The pedal should slowly rise.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brake pedal three times. Then press firmly for five seconds. The pedal should not move.
questions.explanation: Test hydraulic brakes by pumping the brake pedal three times, then pressing firmly for five seconds. The pedal should stay still. If it moves, you may have a leak or other brake system problem.

questions.question: On long trips, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Take breaks to rest.
questions.explanation: Take a break every 100 miles or every two hours of driving to avoid fatigue. Driving at night or when you would normally sleep increases the risk of fatigue.

questions.question: Which item is NOT part of an air brake system?
questions.correctAnswerText: Air filter.
questions.explanation: Air brake systems include an air compressor, storage tanks, gauges, warning devices, valves, and brake controls. An air filter is not part of the air brake system.

questions.question: During your driving test, the examiner scores you on:

options.text: How fast you reach your destination.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your driving behavior.
questions.explanation: The examiner scores you on specific driving maneuvers and your overall driving behavior during the test.

questions.question: Blocking cargo:

options.text: Should only be done in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops cargo from sliding.
questions.explanation: Blocking is a method used to prevent cargo from moving or sliding during transport.

questions.question: To transport hazardous materials, you must pass which endorsement test?
questions.correctAnswerText: Hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: You need a hazardous materials endorsement to drive any vehicle that carries hazardous materials.

questions.question: Driving at night is usually:

options.text: Harder than driving during the day.
Easier than driving during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder than driving during the day.
questions.explanation: Night driving is harder because visibility is reduced, headlight glare affects vision, and more tired drivers are on the road.

questions.question: A 40-foot load needs at least ____ tie-downs.
questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: Use one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. All cargo must have at least two tie-downs, regardless of size.

questions.question: When backing up on your driver's side:

options.text: Is only recommended if it is raining.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is always encouraged.
questions.explanation: Back toward your driver's side when you must back up. This gives you the best view of where you are going.

questions.question: When a train is approaching a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Try to cross the tracks quickly.
Stop and wait for the train to pass before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait for the train to pass before crossing.
questions.explanation: Never try to cross ahead of a train. It is hard to judge how fast a train is moving. Stop and wait for the train to completely pass before you cross the tracks.

questions.question: A single vehicle with air brakes should leak no more than ____ in one minute during a static leakage test.
questions.correctAnswerText: 2 psi
questions.explanation: During a static leakage test, air should not leak more than 2 psi in one minute. Faster leaking means the brakes need repair and the vehicle should not be driven.

questions.question: On slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Speed up and slow down often.
Adjust your speed for the weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Adjust your speed for the weather.
questions.explanation: Match your speed to slippery conditions. Your vehicle takes longer to stop on slippery roads. Leave more distance between you and other vehicles. Avoid changing speeds often.

questions.question: To keep normal stopping power, set a front brake limiting valve to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Normal.
questions.explanation: Some older vehicles have a brake limiting valve with "normal" and "slippery" settings. Always keep it on "normal." The "slippery" setting reduces stopping power. Front wheel braking works well in all conditions.

questions.question: Dry bulk tanks:

options.text: Usually have low centers of gravity.
Usually have high centers of gravity.
Are usually not allowed to cross railroad tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually have high centers of gravity.
questions.explanation: Dry bulk tanks have high centers of gravity and the load can shift while driving. This requires extra care.

questions.question: When an S-cam turns inside a brake drum, it:

options.text: Presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
Presses the brake shoes against the brake linings.
Presses the brake linings against the wheel axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, the S-cam turns and presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum. This creates friction and slows the vehicle.

questions.question: A tired driver:

options.text: Is usually more careful than other drivers.
May be slower to make important decisions.

questions.correctAnswerText: May be slower to make important decisions.
questions.explanation: Tired drivers see and react to hazards slower than rested drivers. Drowsy driving impairs your ability to make quick decisions.

questions.question: You may be driving aggressively if you:

options.text: Slow down and keep a safe distance from other cars.
Make hand gestures that could anger other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make hand gestures that could anger other drivers.
questions.explanation: Avoid aggressive driving by planning for delays, keeping a safe following distance, and not making angry hand gestures at other drivers.

questions.question: Blocking is used to:

options.text: Keep cargo in a large box.
Stop cargo from sliding in a trailer.
Stop cargo from falling out of a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop cargo from sliding in a trailer.
questions.explanation: Blocking is placed on all sides of cargo to keep it from sliding while the vehicle moves.

questions.question: If the low pressure warning light comes on while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Stop where you are and park.
Leave the road as soon as it is safe and park.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave the road as soon as it is safe and park.
questions.explanation: If the low pressure warning light comes on while driving, you must safely leave the road and park as soon as possible. If air pressure gets too low, your brakes will not work well enough to stop safely.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a good rule for using turn signals?

options.text: Signal early. Signal well before you turn or change lanes.
Signal the whole time. Do not stop signaling until your turn is complete.
Do not over-signal. If no one is near you, you do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not over-signal. If no one is near you, you do not need to signal.
questions.explanation: You should always signal before turning or changing lanes. Signal early, signal the whole time you are turning or changing lanes, and turn off the signal when the move is done. Always signal, even if no one is near.

questions.question: When stopping, the brake pedal should be:

options.text: Pressed down quickly with both feet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pressed down slowly.
questions.explanation: Push the brake pedal down slowly to stop the vehicle smoothly and safely.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with air brakes, you should check that the ____ turn on automatically when air pressure drops below 45 psi.
questions.correctAnswerText: Spring brakes
questions.explanation: Before driving, check that spring brakes turn on automatically when air tank pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. Block the wheels and release air by pressing and releasing the brake pedal. When pressure gets too low, the parking brake valve pops out and spring brakes turn on.

questions.question: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, what should you do?

options.text: Leave the vehicle and call for help.
Keep trying to get your vehicle off the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave the vehicle and call for help.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, leave immediately and move away from the tracks. Look for emergency contact information on the signposts at the crossing and call 911 or another emergency number.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, it is important to:

options.text: Put as little weight as possible over the axles.
Spread the weight evenly over the axles.
Put weight only over the axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spread the weight evenly over the axles.
questions.explanation: Cargo must be balanced properly. Too much weight over one axle can damage it and make steering harder. Too little weight over one axle reduces traction and makes handling difficult.

questions.question: Do not drive if any brake drum has a crack larger than ____ of the friction area's width.
questions.correctAnswerText: One half
questions.explanation: Check the brake drums during your inspection before each trip. It is unsafe to drive if any brake drum has a crack larger than one half of the friction area's width.

questions.question: While driving, you should:

options.text: Watch the gauges for signs of problems.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the gauges for signs of problems.
questions.explanation: Watch your vehicle's gauges while driving to spot problems early. Check that all gauges work properly before you start driving.

questions.question: A cargo van is usually:

options.text: The same height whether it has a light or heavy load.
Taller with a heavy load than with a light load.
Shorter with a heavy load than with a light load.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shorter with a heavy load than with a light load.
questions.explanation: A heavy load makes the vehicle sit lower than normal. A vehicle is taller when carrying a light load than when fully loaded. If your full vehicle fits under an overpass, it may not fit when empty.

questions.question: The heavier a vehicle is:

options.text: The less important the brakes become.
The harder the brakes must work.
The quieter the brakes will sound.

questions.correctAnswerText: The harder the brakes must work.
questions.explanation: Heavy vehicles require brakes to work harder to stop. The more weight a vehicle has, the more braking power is needed.

questions.question: What is the best advice for driving in fog?
questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid driving in fog.
questions.explanation: Fog is always dangerous and should be avoided when possible. If you must drive in fog, use low beam headlights and fog lights, even during the day.

questions.question: If you do not drain air tanks, what can happen?

options.text: Water can freeze and cause brake failure.
Too much air collects in the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water can freeze and cause brake failure.
questions.explanation: Air brake system tanks must be drained regularly to remove water and compressor oil. Water that is not removed can freeze in cold weather and cause brakes to fail.

questions.question: What cell phone rules apply to commercial vehicle drivers?

options.text: You can use any cell phone while driving.
You can only use a hands-free cell phone while driving, if allowed.
You can only use a cell phone on rural roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can only use a hands-free cell phone while driving, if allowed.
questions.explanation: If you use a cell phone while driving a commercial vehicle, it must be hands-free and located close to you. Even a hands-free phone can be distracting. Know the cell phone laws in your state.

questions.question: What should you do when stopped on the side of the road?

options.text: Keep the driver's side door open.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on the emergency flashers.
questions.explanation: Use your four-way emergency flashers when stopped on the side of the road. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: What is the average driver's reaction time?
questions.correctAnswerText: 3/4 of a second
questions.explanation: The average driver's reaction time is between three-quarters of a second and one full second. At 55 mph, this means you travel about 61 feet before reacting.

questions.question: What does a ramp's posted speed limit mean for large commercial vehicles?

options.text: It is safe for all vehicles.
It may be too fast for large commercial vehicles.
It is just a suggestion and can be exceeded.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may be too fast for large commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Speed limits on exit and entrance ramps are safe for cars but may be too fast for large or loaded commercial vehicles. Commercial drivers often need to go slower than the posted limit.

questions.question: What is distracted driving?

options.text: Only happens when doing something physical while driving.
Can happen from mental activities like daydreaming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can happen from mental activities like daydreaming.
questions.explanation: Distractions can be physical (reaching for objects), mental (talking with a passenger), or both (texting on a phone). Avoid distractions by pre-programming radio stations, planning your route ahead, avoiding intense conversations, adjusting mirrors before driving, and not eating, drinking, or smoking while driving.

questions.question: If you are convicted of a traffic violation, what must you do?

options.text: Place a sign on the back of your vehicle about the conviction.
Give up your CDL for six months.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell your employer within 30 days.
questions.explanation: You must notify your employer within 30 days of any traffic conviction. You must also report it to your state's licensing agency within 30 days if it happened in another state. Parking violations are not included.

questions.question: Steering wheel play of more than ____ makes steering difficult.
questions.correctAnswerText: 10 degrees
questions.explanation: A steering wheel should have no more than 10 degrees of play. This equals about two inches of movement at the rim of a 20-inch wheel. More than this makes steering difficult.

questions.question: When making tight turns, a driver should:

options.text: Open their door for a better view.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check their mirrors.
questions.explanation: You should check your mirrors regularly while driving. Always check them when changing lanes, turning, merging, or making tight turns.

questions.question: Before a trip, check that:

options.text: The pedal surfaces are grooved and not worn smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: The pedal surfaces are grooved and not worn smooth.
questions.explanation: Check that nothing blocks the pedals and they work properly. Pedal surfaces should be grooved to provide good grip. Smooth or worn pedals are unsafe.

questions.question: When checking your tires, avoid finding:

options.text: Tire tread 4/32 of an inch deep.

questions.correctAnswerText: Different tire sizes.
questions.explanation: Front tires need at least 4/32 inch of tread. Other tires need at least 2/32 inch. Valve stems must not be cut or cracked. All tires should be the same size.

questions.question: Hazardous cargo placards must be placed:

options.text: Only on the front of the vehicle.
On the front, rear, and both sides of the vehicle.
Only on the driver's side of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the front, rear, and both sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Placards must be visible from any direction. Place them on the front, rear, and both sides of the vehicle.

questions.question: Leaf springs should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Not have broken leaves.
questions.explanation: Check that leaf springs have no missing or broken leaves. If one-fourth or more of the leaves are missing, the vehicle must not be driven until it is fixed.

questions.question: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS):

options.text: Work with other braking systems and do not change braking power.
Do not work on larger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work with other braking systems and do not change braking power.
questions.explanation: ABS works alongside normal brakes and does not increase or decrease braking power. It only activates when wheels are about to lock up.

questions.question: Using a helper when backing up a large vehicle is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Encouraged.
questions.explanation: Backing is dangerous because you cannot see well. Use a helper to watch blind spots whenever possible.

questions.question: When should you adjust mirrors?

options.text: When stopped at a traffic signal

questions.correctAnswerText: Before starting a trip
questions.explanation: Adjust mirrors before you start driving. Make sure any trailer is straight while you adjust the mirrors.

questions.question: Emergency equipment in a vehicle is:

options.text: Only required for vehicles carrying hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required.
questions.explanation: Check for emergency equipment during pre-trip inspection. This includes spare fuses, three reflective warning triangles or flares, and one working fire extinguisher.

questions.question: When alley docking, first:

options.text: Position your vehicle directly in front of the alley.
Back up directly in front of the alley.
Stop parallel to the outer edge of the alley.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop parallel to the outer edge of the alley.
questions.explanation: Pull past the alley and stop parallel to its outer edge. Then back your vehicle straight into the alley parking space.
